Carmen Leggio was born on September 30, 1927 in Tarrytown, New York. He took up the clarinet at age 14 after hearing Artie Shaw, and soon after took up the tenor sax. Carmen was playing with small bands around Westchester County while still in his mid-teens and had already decided on making music his career. A stint in the military led him to Washington, D.C. where he performed with bassist Keter Betts and gathered experience playing for large audiences.

Carmen has played and recorded with Maynard Ferguson, Buddy Rich, Woody Herman and Gene Krupa and also held down one of the tenor chairs with the Thad Jones-Mel Lewis Orchestra. His first love continues to be the small combo and his most recent CD release, entitled “Sax After Midnight,” is an intimate recording of classic standards.
Carmen was interviewed in Tarrytown, New York on October 31, 1998, by Monk Rowe, Director of the Fillius Jazz Archive.
My name is Monk Rowe and we are filming today for the Hamilton College Jazz Archive in Tarrytown, New York. I’m quite pleased to have saxophonist Carmen Leggio with me today.
